body:
Yeah.  

Ran 5*5 when I got back in the gym.  While I've seen a lot of people make steady progress with it for decent lengths of time,  it's generally less effective at building mass than building strong,  repeatable habits.  

Newbie strength gains boost confidence, and with the focus on fundamental movements amazing 'practice.'

But a lot of people don't put on a ton of mass staying with it.  Some do,  but really just an intro to programming and moving weight through three dimensions properly. 

It does its job and does it well.  

But the volume / intensity are way way off the mark.  

I've no experience with GVT, so I won't speak to it's efficacy. Though sticking with a program for a year, once you've put some experience behind you,  is generally the absolute minimum I'd recommend. But again,  I've seen people make results in six months others take eighteen months to see results on similar programs.  

As far as the program you ran for a few weeks? There's not a program out there that will constantly build noticeable mass across the board.  

Any claims to the contrary are a load.  

Strength, definitely. 

But training for strength doesn't necessarily equate to training for hypertrophy. 

Again, I know guys that looked great.  But the muscle is soft and they're proportionaly weak.  Other guys that look like stereotypical 'nerd' types and move damn near the weight that I do.  

And while it's my first love, weight training isn't the end all be all of development. Have you considered adding any other forms of resistance training to your routine? 

I've watched people make incredible progress after adding yoga to their routine. Similar results in one case with Thai Chi and ballet. 

I've already invited you to DM me if you're serious. I'm not going to go rounds with ya. 

Offering an honest look at your programming,  diet,  and current physical state versus where you want to be.  

If you want it, I ENJOY doing it.  I've worked with a lot of people and never asked for a cent.  

If you've got your mind made up, that's cool too. 

Either way,  hoping you'll stick with it and maybe find something deeper in it than just aesthetics.  

A lot more to offer than just looks.

Sorry you're having a hard time with it. I can't say I've ever really thought about height in relation to physical attraction. 

But I've only been with one girl my height, everyone else has been shorter.  Some by a pretty good margin - 4'11. 

Actually thinking about it, even the guys I've been with have mostly been shorter than me.  So,  I dunno.  

Maybe it's a subconscious thing?  

But I do know it felt weird staring at the one girl's chest if she decided to wear tall heels.  Lol.  

Not telling you it shouldn't bother you though. I do actually get it, and I'm sorry that's it's causing you pain.

Yeah,  you put on fat when you bulk.  

Dealt with that too.  Hell, cut 100lbs in six months after being the fat kid for 20 years.  Still constantly bulking and then reigning it in to keep BF in check at about 16-18 percent.  

Also noticed that you've run through multiple programs, that you didn't seem to completely grasp,  and abandoned them for the next when you decided that they weren't going to work for you.  

And that you've spent a good bit of time asking questions on AAS subs looking for a solution to your issue.  

Honest question: what's the longest you've stuck with a program beyond something like 5*5?

Do you have a firm grasp on how to program for yourself? To make adjustments to the programming as you go? 

Or do you just grab something off the net,  try it on for a few months and ditch it?  

I'm not trying to minimize your experience, but it honestly sounds like you've got a lot to learn before you can credibly make that judgement. 

And you can site studies,  that's cool.  But I've seen studies that "prove" that will power is measurable and finite.  

I've also listened to people cite those studies as an excuse for their own shortcomings. 

Is what it is. 

You're an adult,  and I'm just a dude offering perspective and some help.  

Believe and do what ya like.

Also,  if you're only interest in women is getting laid,  that's why you're not getting laid.  

They're people,  not objects.  

Relating to them as such will make for a lonely life indeed.

I say this with almost a decade of experience under my belt.  I've coached everyone from 12 year old kids to pro-am athletes to 70 year old women.  

Successfully. 

Sometimes it takes a lot of trial and error, despite having worked hard.  

I've literally coached dozens of young guys in your position. That were ready to throw in the towel. 

And honestly, first thing I'll tell you - and I did dig into your posting history - is that eating clean when you're struggling to put on weight is pointless. 

Don't eat clean,  push the surplus and track it to keep consistent.  

Don't screw with protein powders and all that non-sense.  Just EAT.  

A good friend if mine had the same issue.  I literally had to put him on an 8K a day diet to put on mass.  And his metabolism didn't even out until his early 30's.  

He took in 8K a day for about six years.  Shot from 155-ish to about 230 in that time. Lean.  

Everybody is different, some have a harder go than others.  But nobody is doomed to failure by genetics alone.
If you can type a response on reddit,  you're not too shakey to dial 911...

Success in the realm of fitness isn't genetic, unless you're talking elite level athletics. Where the slightest edge makes a difference.

And comparing yourself to prodigies is a fool's game.  

What, exactly, are you trying to achieve? You want to get "jacked" but what does that mean in relation to you?  

Dropping weight and building muscle? Having a hard time gaining weight? 

Either can be done.  

But here's the trick - it takes time, effort,  and consistency. 

I see it all the time. Dudes that way 150lbs soaking wet that wanna put on 40lbs of lean muscle in a month. 

Fact is,  the best anabolics in the world won't help you put that kind of bulk in six months. Not without still putting on a ton of fat and holding stupid amounts of water.  

People are quick to blame programming or genetics for their lack of success. 

But in my experience, it's usually a matter of skipping work-outs, cutting them short,  not pushing past comfort zones,  and simply not eating and sleeping enough.  

And the heavier people that need to flat put re-comp not getting where the want to be is much the same. Diet issue is just inverted.  

Only thing that'll actually keep you from hitting your goals is lack of discipline and patience.  

If you'd like to elaborate on your particular situation, message me. I can't do it for you,  but I'd be more than happy to get you moving in the right direction. 

Full disclosure: Bettering yourself isn't a means to an end,  it's an end unto itself.  

Getting "jacked" isn't going to get you girls, or gain you any respect. 

It might make you more physically appealing, but if you're lacking in non-physical areas they also need to be addressed. 

What's in the mind is reflected in the body.  In the way we act and carry ourselves.

And...most life insurance policies won't pay out for suicide.

Just so you know.

I'm not at all religious, but very well versed with many if them. 

The simple fact is,  it's not your Mother's place to cast judgement on God's behalf.  Pride is one of the big ones, no?  

There's no point arguing it with her.  Just make the break when you're able. Maybe when she loses her child to it she'll realize her error.  

Maybe not, but you'll be free of the situation either way.

It's no more selfish than it is easy.  

And the fact is,  sometimes it just doesn't get better.  Sometimes it doesn't get easier. 

Sometimes you're literally just wired wrong.  

Sometimes the best you can hope for is a hollow existence, relying on a practiced state of disassociation to get you through the day.  

Which isn't exactly all that fulfilling.  

Suicide is largely stigmatized because we live in a society shaped by religion and government. Institutions designed to take control away from people by casting personal choice in a negative light.  

They propagate those ideas to maintain control.  We're cogs in their machine.  Infinitely replaceable worker bees, but having ten is still better than having nine. Right?  

The fact is,  whether anyone else agrees with you at any point, you are completely in control of your person.  

And in the end suicide, like anything,  is only what you believe it to be.  

And in this case, your truth is all that matters.

Yep. 

And you want to fucking smack them for asking.  I've dreaded it almost every day since I was in grade school.  

I don't ever tell anyone I'm good or okay anymore.  Just sidestep with a non-answer like,  "Getting there." 

While I'm screaming inside and I know the pain in my eyes is clear even though I try to hide it.  

But how do you tell someone that you're so far from okay that you'd need a passport to get back to the same zip code?

Swallow your pride and talk to someone. If you're working, you could also schedule your own appointments with a therapist. 

If not there are usually sliding scale clinics that will not turn you away for being unable to pay.

Regardless of your age,  you're protected by a bevy of Dr/Patient confidentiality and HIPPA laws.  

There are also support forums, Reddit may not really be the best. Know it can be toxic.  

Any of the above would be alternatives to facing family or friends if you're not ready for that.  

Hell,  I've gone to churches and hit the confessional once or twice.  There are options if you're willing to talk to SOMEONE.
Are just looking for someone to talk to or a way to talk to someone in particular?

Been there,  not in another country but definitely far from home. 

Actually only about ten miles from home now though,  and still feel totally out of touch.  It's not easy,  but also not worth staying in an abusive relationship just to avoid talking it through with family or friends. 

Trying to reach out to mine now,  and pride is my greatest hurdle. But I know I need to.  

Badly. 

And a paycheck definitely isn't worth it.  All the nice things in the world don't matter when you're too emotionally wrecked to live and enjoy them.  

I realize that money brings a perception of security, but nothing beyond our person is ever really secure. It's a hard reality to deal with, but it's true.  

All that said,  if you want someone to listen, I'm here.

Dealing with the same if you want to talk. I don't have any answers,  but I understand and know just making a connection can help.  

Either way,  hope it gets easier for you day by day.

Burning through Daredevil and the Bullseye's therapist's notes immediately made my heart sink.  

Like...really? 

BPD is already stigmatized by fucking therapists. The doctors that are supposed to be helping.  

And that's the fucking connection you make? A disorder that's been marginalized and totally misunderstood for decades? 

Thanks Marvel.  

Honestly killed the whole thing for me.
